items.prompt: White has just taken the pawn on d5 with the knight. Black to move. Find Black's best reply.

claims.statement: Taking the knight with the knight from f6 is the engine's top move by a wide margin (depth 16).
One black piece can take the knight on d5.

hints: How many black pieces can capture the knight on d5?
Only one can. Ask what its departure from f6 opens for White's bishop, and whether Black has an answer ready.
The knight from f6 takes on d5. The bishop on g5 will attack the queen, but Black has a reply.
items.explain: The knight on f6 is the only black piece that can take on d5. When it does, the bishop on g5 attacks the queen, which looks like a disaster for Black; the next step shows why it is not. The engine ranks the recapture far above the quiet moves.

feedback_by_move.c7c6: This leaves the white knight on d5, where it has just won a pawn and attacks several squares. It gives White a free pawn.

items.prompt: White has just taken the queen with the bishop. Black to move. Find the move that comes first.

claims.statement: The bishop check on b4 is the engine's top move; the quiet recapture is far worse (depth 16).
The bishop can go from f8 to b4.

hints: Look at the white king on e1. Which black piece can reach a square that gives check?
The bishop on f8 travels along a diagonal that is empty up to b4. What does it attack from there?
Bishop to b4, check. White's only way out of the check costs the queen.
items.explain: The bishop on f8 has a clear run to b4 (e7, d6 and c5 are empty), and from b4 it checks the king through c3 and d2, which White has emptied. White must answer the check, so Black gets to take the queen on d2 with check before recapturing on d8. The plain recapture on d8 comes out much worse for Black (engine, depth 16).

feedback_by_move.e8d8: Retaking at once leaves White a queen for a knight and a bishop ahead; the check has to come first.

items.prompt: White's a-pawn is on a2. Black to move. Does the check on b4 win material back for Black?

claims.statement: Bb4+ is the engine's top move (depth 16).
After the check and the exchanges the engine puts White between -560 and -350 centipawns (White's view): White is clearly worse.

hints: Find the squares from which the bishop on f8 could check the king.
After the check, count what White can do: can anything capture the bishop on b4?
Nothing can capture it. White must interpose with the queen, and Black takes it.
items.explain: Nothing on the white side attacks b4, so the check cannot be met by taking the bishop. White has to block with the queen, and Black takes it with check before retaking on d8. Yes, the check wins the material back and more.

items.prompt: The same position, except that White's a-pawn is on a3. Black to move. Does the check on b4 still win material back?

claims.statement: After ...Bb4+ a white pawn attacks the bishop (the pawn on a3).
The plain recapture on d8 is the engine's top move (depth 16), and it is still bad for Black.
After Kxd8 the engine puts White between 490 and 740 centipawns (White's view): White is clearly better.

hints: Look at b4 again. Which white pieces or pawns attack that square now?
The pawn on a3 attacks b4. What happens to a bishop that checks there?
The pawn takes the bishop and the check gains nothing.
items.explain: With the pawn on a3, White simply takes the checking bishop, and the in-between move has lost its point. Black has to retake on d8 and is a queen down for two pieces. One pawn move removes one of the four conditions, and the trap is gone.

items.prompt: Black to move after 6.Nf3. Find the queen move that attacks the knight on c3 and pins it against the king.

claims.statement: Qa5 is the engine's top move here (depth 16).
The queen can go from d8 to a5.

hints: The king on e1 and the knight on c3 share a diagonal with a5. Which black piece can reach a5?
The queen on d8 travels along the diagonal d8-a5, which is empty (c7 and b6 are free).
The queen to a5.
items.explain: The queen reaches a5 along the empty diagonal. From a5 she attacks the knight on c3 with the white king on e1 behind it, so the knight cannot leave the line. The engine also ranks this move first at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move after the queen came to a5. Can the knight on c3 capture the pawn on d5 with the knight?

claims.statement: The move Nxd5 is illegal here.
The queen on a5 attacks the knight on c3.

hints: Look at the long diagonal from a5. Which pieces stand on it?
The queen, the knight and the king are on one line, and d2 is empty.
A piece that leaves the line exposes its own king, so the knight cannot move at all.
items.explain: The queen on a5, the knight on c3 and the king on e1 stand on one diagonal with d2 empty. If the knight moved anywhere, the queen would give check to its own king's square, so the move is illegal. The knight is pinned, and it cannot take on d5 or go anywhere else.

items.prompt: White to move after 7.Nd2 Bb4. The knight on d2 is blocking the pin. Find a move that adds a defender to the knight on c3.

claims.statement: Rc1, Qc2 and Qc1 are each within 0.4 pawns of the engine's top choice (depth 16).
The knight retreat to f3 loses at least a knight's worth (depth 16).

hints: Which White piece is holding the position together? What would happen if it moved?
The knight on d2 shields the king from the queen. Choose a move that leaves it where it is and adds protection to c3 or breaks the tension.
Rc1, Qc2 and Qc1 each add a defender of the knight on c3; cxd5 is also fine.
items.explain: The knight on d2 is the only thing between the pinned line and the king, so it should stay. Rc1, Qc2 and Qc1 each guard the knight on c3. (The pawn capture on d5 is also fine, but it does not add a defender.) The tempting retreat to f3 unblocks the line and loses a piece.

feedback_by_move.d2f3: This unblocks the diagonal. The knight on c3 is pinned again, and ...Ne4 wins a piece (three attackers against one defender: the bishop, the knight and the queen behind the bishop).

items.prompt: White has just retreated the knight from d2 to f3. Black to move. Does the knight jump from f6 to e4 win a piece?

claims.statement: The jump to e4 wins at least two points of material against best defence (depth 16).
After the jump two black pieces attack the knight on c3.

hints: Count the attackers of the knight on c3 after the jump, and its defenders.
The bishop and the knight attack c3, the queen stands behind; only the pawn on b2 defends it. Can the knight on c3 take on e4?
No: it is pinned, so Black wins a piece.
items.explain: With the knight back on f3 the diagonal to the king is open, so the knight on c3 is pinned. After the jump it is attacked twice and defended once, and it cannot capture the intruder on e4. The bishop on g5 is attacked as well. Black wins material.

items.prompt: The same position, except that the white knight is still on d2 and it is Black's move. Does the knight jump from f6 to e4 win a piece?

claims.statement: The jump to e4 does not win material against best defence (depth 16): the gain is at most one point.
After the jump two black pieces attack the knight on c3, as in the first position.

hints: Where is the white knight now, and what does it do to the diagonal?
The knight on d2 blocks the line from c3 to the king, so the knight on c3 is free to move.
White can take on e4 with a knight, and the pieces just trade.
items.explain: Black attacks c3 twice in both positions. The difference is the blocker: with the knight on d2 the knight on c3 is not pinned, and the knight on d2 also attacks e4, so White takes the intruder and the pieces trade evenly. The same jump works or fails depending on one blocker.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's knight has just jumped from f6 to d5. Two white pieces are attacked. Find a move that deals with both.

claims.statement: Bxe7, h4, Nxd5 and Bf4 are all within 0.4 pawns of the best move at depth 16.
Qc2 ignores both threats and loses at least a piece (depth 16).

hints: Name the two white pieces that are attacked, and the black pieces that attack them.
The knight on c3 is attacked by the knight on d5, and the bishop on g5 by the bishop on e7. One move must meet both, or remove one of the attackers first.
Trade the attacked bishop (Bxe7), trade the knight (Nxd5), back up the bishop with the h-pawn, or move it to f4.
items.explain: The knight on d5 attacks the knight on c3, and by leaving f6 it opens the line from the bishop on e7 to the bishop on g5. A good reply must take care of both: trade a piece (Bxe7 or Nxd5), support the bishop (h4) or move it (Bf4). Quiet developing moves such as Qc2 lose a piece.

feedback_by_move.d1c2: Qc2 ignores the bishop: ...Bxg5 Nxg5 Qxg5 wins a piece, and the knight on d5 still attacks c3.
feedback_by_move.e1g1: Castling ignores the bishop: ...Bxg5 Nxg5 Qxg5 wins a piece.

items.prompt: The black queen is on d8, behind the bishop on e7. White to move. Does the quiet developing move Qc2 lose a piece?

claims.statement: Qc2 loses at least a piece compared with the best move (depth 16).
One black piece attacks the bishop on g5 directly (the bishop on e7); the queen stands behind it.

hints: Count the attackers of the bishop on g5, and the defenders.
The bishop on e7 attacks it, and the queen on d8 is lined up behind the bishop. The knight on f3 is the only defender.
Two attackers against one defender: White loses a piece.
items.explain: The bishop on e7 attacks g5, and the queen on d8 stands behind it on the same diagonal. The knight on f3 is the only defender, so after the trades on g5 the queen takes the knight. Qc2 loses a piece.

items.prompt: The same position, except that the black queen stands on e8, not on d8. White to move. Does the quiet developing move Qc2 lose a piece?

claims.statement: After Qc2 the engine puts the position between -50 and 110 centipawns from White's side: about level.
One black piece attacks the bishop on g5 (the bishop on e7), with nothing lined up behind it.

hints: Count the attackers of the bishop on g5 again. What stands behind the bishop on e7 this time?
The queen is on e8, not on d8, so the diagonal behind the bishop is empty.
One attacker against one defender: after the trades on g5 nothing more is hitting the knight.
items.explain: With the queen on e8 the bishop on e7 attacks g5 only once, and the knight on f3 defends it. After the trades on g5 no black piece is left to take the knight, so Qc2 does not lose a piece. The line behind the bishop was the whole difference.

items.prompt: White has retreated the bishop to d3, next to the knight on f3. Black to move. Does the pawn push ...e4 win a piece?

claims.statement: The pawn push wins at least two points of material against best defence (depth 16).
The push ...e4 is the engine's top move (depth 16).

hints: Which two white pieces stand on squares a pawn on e4 would attack?
The bishop is on d3 and the knight on f3. Is e4 guarded? Can White take the pawn profitably?
The queen guards the pawn, so Bxe4 Qxe4 wins a bishop for a pawn. White loses a piece.
items.explain: A black pawn on e4 would attack both d3 and f3, and the queen on e7 guards it. If the bishop takes, the queen retakes and White has lost a bishop for a pawn; if White moves one piece, the pawn takes the other. White loses a piece for a pawn.

items.prompt: This time the bishop has retreated to b3. Black to move. Does the pawn push ...e4 win a piece?

claims.statement: The pawn push wins no more than one point of material (depth 16).
After ...e4 one black piece attacks the knight on f3 (the pawn on e4).

hints: Which white pieces would the pawn attack after ...e4 this time?
The bishop on b3 is not on d3 or f3. Only the knight on f3 is attacked.
The knight simply steps away (for example to d2), and Black has gained nothing.
items.explain: With the bishop on b3 only the knight on f3 stands on a square the pawn would attack. The knight can step away to d2 and the pawn on e4 has gained space, nothing more. The same push is a fork or a nuisance depending on where the bishop stands.

items.prompt: White to move. Does the knight capture 9.Nxd5 win a pawn?

claims.statement: The capture on d5 loses at least a piece compared with the best move (depth 16).
Four black pieces guard the pawn on d5 (the pawns on c6 and e6, the knight on f6 and the queen along the fifth rank).

hints: Count the guards of the pawn on d5.
Pawns on c6 and e6, the knight on f6 and the queen along the fifth rank. Now count what the knight on c3 is doing for the king.
The pawn is guarded, and the knight leaving c3 lets the bishop and queen into the diagonal. No.
items.explain: The pawn on d5 is guarded by two pawns, a knight and the queen, so a knight for a pawn is a bad trade on its own; the knight also leaves c3, which unblocks the diagonal to the bishop on b4 and the queen. The capture loses a piece.

items.prompt: White to move. The bishop on c4 is going to retreat. Which retreat loses a piece: the bishop to d3 or the bishop to b3?

claims.statement: Bd3 loses at least a piece compared with the best move (depth 16).
After Bb3 the engine puts the position between -40 and 130 centipawns (White's view): it is level.

hints: Look at Black's last move, e5. What could that pawn do next?
Check each retreat square: which pieces would end up on squares that a black pawn could attack?
Bd3: the pawn then attacks bishop and knight.
items.explain: A black pawn on e4 would attack d3 and f3. The knight already stands on f3, so a bishop on d3 completes a pawn fork; b3 does not. The engine confirms that Bd3 loses a piece and Bb3 is level.

items.prompt: White to move. Which of these moves is the mistake: the rook to c1, the queen to c2 or the knight back to f3?

claims.statement: Nf3 loses at least a knight's worth compared with the best move (depth 16).
Rc1 and Qc2 are both fine (within 0.4 pawns of the best move, depth 16).

hints: Which White piece is blocking the diagonal to the king?
Which of the three moves moves that piece?
The knight back to f3 unblocks the pin.
items.explain: Rc1 and Qc2 leave the blocker on d2 and add protection. The retreat to f3 moves the blocker, the pin returns, and the knight jump to e4 wins a piece.

items.prompt: White to move after the knight jumped to d5. One of these moves loses a piece: the bishop takes on e7, the knight takes on d5, or the queen goes to c2. Which one?

claims.statement: Qc2 loses at least a piece compared with the best move (depth 16).
Bxe7 and Nxd5 are both fine (within 0.4 pawns of the best, depth 16).

hints: Which two white pieces are attacked?
Which of the three moves does nothing about either attack?
Qc2: the bishop on g5 is lost.
items.explain: Bxe7 removes one attacker and Nxd5 trades the attacked knight; both leave White fine. Qc2 develops a piece but leaves the bishop on g5 attacked twice (bishop and queen) and defended once, and it loses a piece.
